definitions.explanation: Conversation that serves no productive purpose. Can be mildly negative (wasting time) or neutral (casual socializing), depending on context.

examples.japanese: {無駄話|むだばなし}はやめて{仕事|しごと}をしなさい。
examples.english: Stop chatting and get to work.

examples.japanese: {同僚|どうりょう}と{無駄話|むだばなし}をしていたら{上司|じょうし}に{注意|ちゅうい}された。
examples.english: I was scolded by my boss for chitchatting with a colleague.

examples.japanese: たまには{無駄話|むだばなし}でもしながらのんびり{過|す}ごすのもいい。
examples.english: Sometimes it's nice to spend time relaxing and just chatting about nothing.

notes:
USAGE:
{無駄話|むだばなし} implies the conversation has no particular point or purpose. In work settings it is negative (time-wasting), but socially it can be neutral or even positive (enjoying casual conversation).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {無駄話|むだばなし}をする (to make idle talk)
- {無駄話|むだばなし}が{多|おお}い (to talk too much idly)
- {無駄話|むだばなし}はやめろ (stop the chitchat)

WORD FORMATION:
{無駄|むだ} (futile, pointless) + {話|はなし} (talk). The は becomes ば through rendaku.

SIMILAR WORDS:
{雑談|ざつだん} (casual conversation) is more neutral and common. {おしゃべり} (chatting) is lighthearted. {無駄話|むだばなし} specifically emphasizes the lack of purpose.
